## February 20, 1952

You arrived on a Wednesday, in the deep cold of an Olympic winter.

---

**The Games were happening right now.** The 1952 Winter Olympics in Oslo, Norway were in full swing — they ran February 14 through 25 — and on the exact day you were born, the world's best athletes were competing on Norwegian snow and ice. It was the first time the Winter Games had been held in Scandinavia since 1936, and the first postwar Winter Olympics in Europe. The world was watching sport again, a hopeful signal after the devastation of the previous decade.

**Fourteen days earlier, a new queen.** On February 6, 1952 — just two weeks before your birth — King George VI died in his sleep at Sandringham. His daughter Elizabeth, 25 years old, became Queen of the United Kingdom while on safari in Kenya. She hadn't yet been told when you arrived. The Elizabethan age that would define half a century of British culture, Commonwealth politics, and global monarchy had just quietly begun. You would live 70 of the 70 years of her reign, from her accession to her death in 2022.

**You were born into the Korean War.** The armistice wouldn't come until July 1953 — your first fourteen months of life unfolded while American soldiers were dying in a conflict that had no clear end in sight. Harry Truman, deeply unpopular over the war and a cascade of political scandals, would announce two weeks later that he would not seek re-election. The November election would bring Dwight Eisenhower — "I Like Ike" — and a transition that reshaped American political identity for a generation.

**The nuclear shadow was already permanent.** The Soviet Union had tested its first atomic bomb in 1949. By 1952, both superpowers were racing toward the hydrogen bomb — the US would test one in November of that very year, a weapon roughly 500 times more powerful than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima. You grew up in the first generation to live entirely under the possibility of civilizational annihilation. That shadow, present on the day you were born, would never fully lift during the Cold War decades that shaped your formative years.

**Television was remaking the world you'd grow up in.** In 1952, roughly 15 million television sets were in American homes — a number that would triple by the end of the decade. You were young enough to grow up with TV as simply part of life, not a novelty. The medium that would carry the civil rights movement into living rooms, broadcast the moon landing, define political campaigns, and eventually evolve into the internet-connected screens in every pocket — it was just hitting its stride when you arrived.

---

**Your tenth birthday was extraordinary.** On February 20, 1962 — your exact birthday, ten years to the day — John Glenn climbed into a capsule called Friendship 7 and became the first American to orbit the Earth. He circled the globe three times in under five hours. You turned ten on the day America caught up in the space race, a morning the country held its breath and then exhaled with collective pride. Few birthdays in the twentieth century share their exact date with a moment that clear.

---

**The lifetime arc.** You were born into a world of typewriters, party-line telephones, and milk delivered to the door. The country you arrived in had 150 million people and was just beginning to build its Interstate highways. By the time you were 17, humans had walked on the moon. At 37, you watched the Berlin Wall fall and the Cold War's long freeze end. At 49, you watched two towers collapse and the world reorganize around a new kind of threat. At 68, a pandemic shut down the planet. Now, at 74, machines are writing, composing, reasoning, and the question of what it means for humans to think is being renegotiated in real time.

---

You entered a world rebuilding itself after catastrophe, cautiously hopeful, newly dangerous at a nuclear scale, and still innocent of everything that was about to transform it — rock and roll, televised politics, the counterculture, the digital revolution, the internet, the phone that became a portal. The person born on February 20, 1952 is someone who has genuinely witnessed the world remake itself, not once but several times over. That is not a small thing to have lived.
